rationale: unit:shared.resolution matches lean:Shared/Step:Resolve and lean:Shared/State:Mode.join. Resolve.variable reads an initialized variable reference and reports its own mode. Resolve.field first resolves the base, requires the containing object to be present, then requires an initialized named field and joins the accumulated mode with the stored field mode. Mode.join returns unique only for two unique arguments. Thus a shared reference in the middle cannot be forgotten when a later field is unique, and missing variables, fields, intermediate objects or initialized contents prevent the corresponding derivation. Resolve has one fixed state parameter and no output state, matching the claim that reading the route changes nothing. The prose carefully requires intermediate objects, not an extra final-object allocation check absent from this relation.
